key_insight: Encoder--decoder operator learning can be analyzed in a resolution-independent way by passing to a limiting kernel, so approximation, regularization, and optimization effects can be separated cleanly.
engineering_relevance: This gives practical error and complexity guarantees for neural operator models built from finite-resolution data, including how performance scales with encoding resolution, step size, width, and sample size.
method: Induce an operator-valued kernel on function spaces from a matrix-valued kernel on encoded data.
Prove convergence of the induced kernels to a limiting kernel via operator-norm convergence of the associated integral operators.
Extend the analysis to regularized SGD and wide encoder--decoder neural networks through the limiting NTK.
evidence_signal: The paper provides upper and lower theoretical bounds for regularized SGD and NTK-based encoder--decoder networks, including polynomial complexity guarantees when encoding errors decay algebraically.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on asymptotic kernel convergence and encoding-error decay, so finite-resolution encoders or strongly nonideal discretizations may weaken the stated rates.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
